title: Towards fault-tolerance with universal phase-error-transparent gates for high-spin cat codes
authors: Kelvin Onggadinata, Si Yan Koh, Arghya Maity, Kuan Eng Johnson Goh, Bent Weber, Kay Jin Lim, Hui Khoon Ng, Teck Seng Koh
abstract: High-dimensional nuclear spins offer a hardware-efficient route to quantum error correction (QEC), with the spin cat code providing intrinsic robustness against phase errors -- the dominant noise channel in donor-in-silicon architectures. However, realizing the full potential of this encoding requires gate operations that preserve its error-correcting properties. In this work, we construct a universal logical gate set that is error-transparent (ET) to phase errors, and discuss its practical implementations and challenges. The ET gates ensure that phase errors occurring stochastically during gate operations are propagated in a systematically traceable manner and remain correctable in a subsequent QEC step. Among the universal gate set constructed, we identify the logical $X$ gate as the primary challenge and discuss potential realization schemes. In addition, to fully leverage the spin cat code's advantage over an unencoded qubit, multi-tone microwave driving of the logical $CZ$ gate is essential. Our simulations show that ET gates significantly outperform non-ET gates and may be necessary to surpass the break-even point. We further show how logical measurement and recovery can be constructed from ET operations, and explain why state-preparation cannot be made ET. In particular, ET measurement in the computational basis is realizable via spin parity measurement, and that error correction circuits constructed from ET operations achieve optimal error correction capacity. Our work charts a concrete path toward full fault-tolerant quantum computation with high-dimensional nuclear spin systems.
summary: This paper develops the theory required to achieve fault-tolerant quantum computing using high-dimensional nuclear spins encoded in a spin cat code. The core contribution is the construction of universal logical gates that are 'Error-Transparent' (ET) to phase errors, ensuring that operational noise remains correctable by subsequent Quantum Error Correction steps. This provides a concrete path toward scalable quantum computation in solid-state systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is constructing quantum gates for high-dimensional nuclear spin systems that are fault-tolerant against phase errors, which dominate noise in donor-in-silicon architectures.
main_result: The authors construct a universal set of Error-Transparent (ET) logical gates and demonstrate that ET operations are crucial for achieving optimal error correction capacity necessary for full fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The work involves theoretical construction of gate sets, formalizing the Error Transparency criterion ($\left[\hat{\mathcal{E}}_j, \hat{H}(t)ight]|\psi_Langle= 0$), and analyzing the fault tolerance of measurement and error correction gadgets.
model_or_system: The system utilizes high-dimensional nuclear spins (e.g., in donor atoms in silicon) encoded into a spin cat code, which provides intrinsic robustness against phase errors. Control is achieved via ESR and NMR/NER driving fields.
key_observables: Error propagation paths, fault counts ($t(I), t(A), t(O)$), logical gate fidelity relative to ET vs non-ET gates, and measurement POVM operators (CAN, DUAL).
important_parameters: The code distance $p = 2r + 1$ and the error order $r$, which dictates the maximum correctable error weight.
main_assumptions: Errors are primarily modeled as dephasing errors ($\hat{I}_z$), and the analysis relies on constructing gates that satisfy the ET criterion for fault tolerance across all components (gates, measurement, correction).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy level diagrams showing ESR/NMR control; one figure contrasts ET vs non-ET operations; another details the implementation of a logical CZ gate using multiple conditioned pulses.
paper_structure: The paper develops from establishing the physical platform and error model, to constructing the universal set of ET gates (including $Z(	heta)$ and $CZ$), and finally proving fault tolerance for measurement and error correction circuits based on these ET operations.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly detailed theoretical roadmap for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation in solid-state spin qubits, directly addressing the critical issue of noise resilience in physical implementations.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Diagram of the donor and electron system in sil- icon and their energy levels. The eigenstates |s⟩⊗|I, mI⟩ are split into two branches with electron spin s =↓(s =↑) corresponding to the lower (upper) branch. Electron spin resonance (ESR) controls inter-branch transitions, while transitions between nuclear spin levels within each branch can be controlled with resonant magnetic fields (NMR). The quadrupole interaction enables transitions via electric fields on resonance with nuclear spacings of ∆mI = ±1 and ∆mI = ±2 (NER±1, NER±2).

FIG. 2: (a) Dephasing errors act as spin ladder operations in the {|I, mI⟩x} basis, with each |mI| forming the support state for the logical subspace and error subspaces. (b) Conceptual illustration of error-transparent (ET) and non-ET operations. The red arrow illustrates the action of an error operator causing jumps from error subspaces of lower rank to higher ones. ET operations preserve the intended trajectories/evolutions in the logical subspace in each of the error subspaces. Performing error correction (represented by green arrow) at any time then brings the transformed state in the error subspaces to the appropriate state in the logical subspace.

FIG. 3: Error-transparent implementation of logical CZ gate for I = 3/2. A sequence of four consecutive ESR- based 2π rotations applied on the electron ancilla pro- duces a geometric phase conditional on the support states of the |1L⟩state, resulting in an ET CZ gate. Each thick blue line corresponds to a high-spin donor (d-level sys- tem) with state labels |nk⟩, k = 1, 2, while the thin black line corresponds to the electron system with state label |e⟩. The ESR frequencies are denoted by ωESR mI,m′ I with mI, m′ I being the conditional spin states on n1, n2, re- spectively.

FIG. 5: Knill error correction (Knill-EC) circuit based on teleportation. All the rails of the circuit are assumed to be the same high-spin system (denoted with blue thick lines) that is encoded in spin cat-x code. The data rail contains a noisy logical state represented by the error channel N acting on ρL, while the ancilla and output rail are initialized in the logical dual state |+L⟩. The re- maining circuit components consists of ET version of CZ gates, logical dual basis measurements, and appropriate Pauli gates depending on the measurement outcomes.
